ambiguities: Legrandin delivers a melancholic farewell speech quoting poetry and addressing the narrator warmly as 'mon jeune ami' and the group as 'les camarades'; this is part of his recurring self-dramatizing, sentimentally literary posturing elsewhere ironized in the work, but this immediate passage contains no explicit narrator judgment (praise, blame, or irony marker) on the performance, so it was left unscored rather than assumed ironic.

Swann is credited as the source of the epithet 'la Charité de Giotto' for the ailing kitchen maid; this shows his characteristic erudite wit but is a passing attribution with no clear local evaluative direction toward Swann himself, so it was not scored as an event.
